neighbours.label: time-unit word after a number in an expression of elapsed time before the present ('N years ago / since', Korean '년 전', Japanese '年'); the - pole is the same unit in 'N years away' (future distance)
fire: The glacier carved this valley roughly twenty thousand years ago.
About sixty years since, the mill was built beside the river.
I visited the old temple a few months ago with my cousin.
몇 년 전에 우리는 그 마을로 이사했다.
The town was founded some three hundred years ago by fishermen.
We last spoke on the phone two weeks ago, just before his trip.
Dinosaurs went extinct about sixty-six million years ago.
He retired from teaching nearly ten years ago.
quiet: Engineers say a working prototype is still a couple of years away.
The election is now only two weeks away and the polls are tight.
The new bridge will take three more years to finish.
The festival lasts five days and draws visitors from across the region.
The nearest hospital is forty miles away over the mountain road.
The contract runs for ten years and can be renewed after that.
Experts think a cure may be decades away despite recent progress.
She plans to study abroad for six months next year.

notes: Card: + pole top ' years' x7, '년' x6, '年' x6 in 'about 14,000 years ago', 'sixty-five years since', '몇 년 전'. - pole: 'a couple of years away', 'a week away'. Logit suppresses 'away'. Near misses use the same units as future distance or duration.
